scope: The eight files named as next by M38 (src/asn1/{evp_asn1,i2d_evp,layout,nsseq,p5_pbe,p5_pbev2,p5_scrypt,p8_pkey}.rs). Contract checks against OpenSSL 3.6.4 for ASN.1 item descriptors and callbacks, allocated-block ownership in the PBE/PBKDF2/scrypt builders, the fixed EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH stack buffers, PKCS#8 private-key octet cleansing and release, and the provided/legacy key DER writer hand-offs. Three genuine defects across three files repaired (one private-key block leak and two unvalidated IV-length overflows); one allocator-seam coordinate corrected. No new unsafe operation or FFI symbol introduced.
worktree: source: src/asn1/p8_pkey.rs, src/asn1/p5_pbev2.rs, src/asn1/p5_scrypt.rs and src/asn1/p5_pbe.rs repaired; src/asn1/{evp_asn1,i2d_evp,layout,nsseq}.rs audited with no source change. queue/receipt: REMAINING-AUDIT.txt, AUDITED-FILES.txt, PERFILE-INDEX.md section 43 and this file.

reconciliation.method: AUDITED-FILES.txt is the union of each mechanism sweep's structured .files array, the M1 files, the structured per-file records and each boundary sweep's structured boundaries. The eight files added here were the first eight entries of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt and were inserted at their existing asn1-block positions (evp_asn1 after der, i2d_evp/layout after i2d, nsseq/p5_pbe/p5_pbev2/p5_scrypt/p8_pkey after new).
reconciliation.difference_from_349: M38 left 349 audited / 414 unaudited. This batch moves the eight files it named as next; no skipped boundary was removed from the remaining queue.

mechanisms: borrowed local ASN1_OCTET_STRING over the caller's buffer
file_dispositions.note: The local octet string is a view of the caller's buffer and is never freed; the unpacked temporary is released exactly once on every arm. The Rust copy guards the authority's unconditional memcpy with n > 0 / non-NULL, which only changes C-invalid inputs (negative copy length or a NULL destination) where the authority has UB. num truncation (long -> int32) is the authority's assignment.

The ENCODER context is released once per chain entry; the temporary PKCS#8 structure is released once after the encode, through the p8_pkey item, so its private-key octets take the FREE_PRE cleanse path (and, before this batch, the leak repaired there). The caller owns every output buffer; no internal secret buffer is copied or retained.

mechanisms: unsafe Sync impls for Asn1Item, Asn1Template, Asn1PrimitiveFuncs and BitStringBitname
file_dispositions.note: Definition-only unit. The four Sync claims cover statics built from scalars, raw pointers and function pointers, written once at load and never mutated through the shared reference; no function or ownership transition lives here.
The callback borrows the process-static OID object exactly as the authority does; ASN1_OBJECT_free refuses the static origin on the release path. Certificate values are public data; no secret buffer.

SaltBuf's failure-path release used the authority's goto line (p5_pbe.c:59) instead of the OPENSSL_free it reaches (p5_pbe.c:76). Corrected so a caller-installed allocator hook observes the authority's free coordinate. Ownership/order (drop salt, then PBEPARAM_free, then packed-string free on set0 refusal) already matched.

The IV copy/draw trusted EVP_CIPHER_get_iv_length into a 16-byte stack array, reachable with a caller-registered method whose iv_len is larger (EVP_CIPHER_meth_set_iv_length). Refused above EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH on the bare err tail, following the cms_enc/pem_bridge precedent. Salt and IV are public AlgorithmIdentifier contents, released plainly.

mechanisms: ASN1_STRING_set for salt (copy or grow), RAND_bytes draw
file_dispositions.note: Same unvalidated iv_len overflow as p5_pbev2, repaired the same way. The salt is copied by ASN1_STRING_set and drawn in place when absent, exactly as the authority; a negative saltlen keeps the authority's strlen semantics. Salt is public, released plainly.

mechanisms: pkey_cb ASN1_OP_FREE_PRE cleanse and ASN1_OP_D2I_POST version contract
file_dispositions.note: ASN1_OP_FREE_PRE cleansed the whole ASN1_STRING object, zeroing the data pointer and length that ASN1_STRING_free reads immediately afterwards; every PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO free therefore leaked the private-key octet block. Only the contents are now cleansed (length clamped to 0), matching p8_pkey.c:27, and a regression test pins that the owner stays releasable.

defects.kind: private-key octet block leaked on every PKCS#8 free
defects.detail: pkey_cb's ASN1_OP_FREE_PRE cleansed size_of::<Asn1String>() bytes at the pkey string itself, so the item layer's subsequent ASN1_STRING_free saw data == NULL and length == 0 and released only the string object. The authority cleanses key->pkey->data for key->pkey->length (p8_pkey.c:27) and leaves the owner intact. Now only the contents are cleansed, clamped at zero.

defects.kind: stack buffer overflow from unvalidated IV length
defects.detail: iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH] (16) was filled with EVP_CIPHER_get_iv_length(cipher) bytes with no upper bound. A caller-registered EVP_CIPHER with a longer iv_len (EVP_CIPHER_meth_set_iv_length) makes both the aiv copy and the RAND draw overrun. The authority has the same overrun; §17 forbids reproducing it. Refused above EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH at the authority's err tail (no authority error site exists on this arm).

defects.kind: stack buffer overflow from unvalidated IV length
defects.detail: Same 16-byte iv array filled with an unchecked EVP_CIPHER_get_iv_length; repaired with the same refusal as p5_pbev2.
SaltBuf released the RAND-failure block at p5_pbe.c:59 (the goto) rather than :76 (the OPENSSL_free at the err tail it reaches). A caller-installed free hook observed the wrong line. Corrected to 76.

secret_buffers.cleansed_on: ASN1_OP_FREE_PRE for every item release (PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free, d2i failure cleanup, ossl_evp_pkey2pkcs8 temporary)
secret_buffers.released_on: the item layer's ASN1_STRING_free immediately after the callback (plain free, matching the authority's OPENSSL_free)
secret_buffers.note: Contents are cleansed and released on all item-free paths. A negative length (possible only through PKCS8_pkey_set0 with penclen < 0, as in the authority) clamps the cleanse to zero instead of the authority's implicit size_t overrun.

secret_buffers.released_on: the owning ASN1 item's free (ASN1_STRING_free / item free), plain
secret_buffers.note: The salt is stored in the public AlgorithmIdentifier alongside the ciphertext; the authority neither cleanses nor clear-frees it. Release arms are preserved: Drop on RAND failure, or ownership transfer to ASN1_STRING_set0/the item.
IVs are public; the security-critical property is the length bound, now enforced.

secret_buffers.buffer: i2d_provided output and legacy DER output
secret_buffers.note: The only secret-bearing temporary on this path is the PKCS#8 structure passed to PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free, which takes the cleanse above.

contracts_reused: RC-1 item descriptor/template layout (offset-asserted repr(C) + static descriptor)
OB-1 release-seam discipline for a bespoke CRYPTO_malloc owner (SaltBuf: one Drop, authority coordinates, into_raw only on adoption)
OB-1/OB-4 ASN1_STRING_set0 ownership transfer and member-buffer release
ASN1 item lifecycle contract (ASN1_item_new / d2i / i2d / ASN1_item_free; callback NEW_POST/D2I_POST/FREE_PRE)
ASN1_OP_D2I_POST version contract (v1 only without kpub; 0..=1)
EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH stack-buffer contract from cms_enc.rs and pem_bridge.rs (refuse ivlen > 16 rather than reproduce the authority overrun)
X509_ALGOR_set0 adoption semantics (failure leaves ownership with the caller on the authority's paths)
ASN1_STRING_set length semantics (negative len = strlen) for the scrypt salt

fast.focused_tests: cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=4 asn1::p8_pkey 4 passed / 0 failed (includes the new FREE_PRE regression); cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=4 asn1:: 40 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored

retained_obligations: p5_scrypt keeps the authority's negative-saltlen strlen semantics: a negative length with a non-NULL salt requires a NUL-terminated readable string

PKCS8_pkey_set0 still accepts a negative penclen exactly as the authority; the cleanse clamps at zero (deliberate divergence from the authority's implicit size_t overrun, no observable allocator event change)
p8_pkey cleanses only the PrivateKey octets, not attribute values, matching the authority
PBE salts and IVs are not cleansed by design (public AlgorithmIdentifier contents)
ivlen > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH is now refused with the bare err tail: a deliberate §17 divergence with no error raise because the authority has no coordinate on that arm
error tails still omit the pointer-bearing ERR_print_errors lines, as established for this crate
